item.title: Cutajar reports TikTok user who praised Cisse’s alleged killers
item.description: Equality Minister Rosianne Cutajar has reported to the police a man who praised two former soldiers accused of murdering Lassane Cisse because he was black. The comment, posted under a Times of Malta video about the 2019 killing, said the alleged shooters were defending their country against trash black people and that it was a pity they killed only one of three men. Cutajars intervention came hours after the trial of one of the accused, Lorin Scicluna, opened with testimony naming his friend as the shooter.

Sources: Times of Malta

item.title: Scicluna told police his friend fired the shot that killed Lassane Cisse, jury hears
item.description: Former soldier Lorin Scicluna told the court that his friend Francesco Fenech was the one who fired the shot that killed Lassane Cisse, the 42-year-old Ivorian worker shot dead in Birżebbuġa in April 2019. CID officer Jeffrey Gerada told jurors that Scicluna was very nervous and took police to various locations he mentioned while under interrogation, including an Attard pastizzi shop where he worked part-time and where he said he had lent his car to a Libyan man. Scicluna, who pleads not guilty, faces nine charges and is also accused of the attempted murder of two other black men shot in the same incident.

item.title: Man walks free after his brother drops the arson case
item.description: Errol Grech walked out of court a free man on Friday after his brother told the court he no longer wished to pursue an arson case against him. The two brothers were charged in 2019 with setting fire to a Volkswagen belonging to a third brother, Rosario Grech, in Żejtun, and Errol Grech was eventually jailed for four years. His conviction was overturned on appeal, and Magistrate Astrid May Grima upheld the victims request, ending the proceedings.

item.title: Aquilina says he is physically threatened in public
item.description: Civil society activist Robert Aquilina said he has been physically threatened and attacked in public as part of a campaign to dehumanise him, comparing it to the campaign against Daphne Caruana Galizia before she was killed. Speaking on a pre-recorded programme, he said Labour supporters have spotted him in public and moved to assault him. Last Wednesday he named the alleged creator of a derogatory AI-generated image of him as Joseph Abela, brother of former judge Toni Abela, saying the information was verified by police.

item.title: Government to strengthen the 1400 helpline and community health services
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Health Minister Ian Borg said the government plans further improvements to the 1400 medical helpline and primary healthcare services to direct patients to the most appropriate care and reduce pressure on Mater Dei Hospitals emergency department. Since July 2025 the 1400 service has assisted more than 59,418 people, averaging 124 patients a day. Planned changes include patient-streamlining at health centres, infrastructure and equipment upgrades, and a new digital system giving callers real-time information.

item.title: Government to back businesses on EU competitiveness, says Azzopardi Tanti
item.description: Minister for European Funds, Social Dialogue and Consumer Protection Keith Azzopardi Tanti addressed a business breakfast marking the 30th anniversary of the Malta Business Bureau, bringing together government, industry and social partners. Discussions focused on digital innovation, adapting to environmental requirements and making EU policy take account of the conditions under which businesses operating on islands function. MBB president Raphael Aloisio said the bureaus early engagement on EU initiatives continues to deliver value for Maltese business.

item.title: Visitor centre planned at the prehistoric Baħrija site
item.description: A year after the Planning Authority rejected a residential proposal on the Baħrija plateau, a new application for a visitor and research centre in the same Bronze Age settlement zone has been submitted. Application PA/7541/26 was filed last month by the Baħrija Foundation, whose website was only registered in July and which does not appear in the Malta Business Registry. The application confirms the foundation is not the property owner but is presenting it with the owners consent.

item.title: Malta embassy in France urges vigilance ahead of demonstrations
item.description: The Embassy of Malta in France has warned Maltese nationals living in or visiting the country to be more vigilant ahead of demonstrations expected on Saturday. The embassy said the protests could cause transport disruptions, road closures and restricted access to some areas, advising nationals to avoid gatherings and allow extra time for journeys. Around 70,000 law enforcement officers are expected to be deployed as protests over the cost of living and crumbling educational infrastructure continue.

item.title: Beekeepers warn the €1m honey bee plan may not be enough
item.description: Beekeeping and environmental organisations welcomed the governments seven-measure, 1 million action plan against the Oriental hornet but warn the funding may be insufficient. They say aid for re-establishing lost colonies should be restricted to the native Maltese honey bee, Apis mellifera ruttneri, and want clarity on how the required proportion of Maltese bees will be verified. The plan also covers compensation for lost honey production and breeding programmes for the native subspecies.

item.title: Solidarjetà: foreign workers are not the cause of traffic and overdevelopment
item.description: The Solidarjetà union says Maltas traffic congestion, overdevelopment and high rents stem from poor planning and regulation rather than from foreign workers. The union, which represents migrant workers and local residents, said foreign workers are essential to healthcare, elderly care, public transport, cleaning, construction and hospitality. It asked the budget due next week to treat migrant workers with the same dignity and respect as others, warning that low wages and poor conditions harm every worker.

item.title: MFSA appoints auditors to take control of Trive’s assets
item.description: The Malta Financial Services Authority has appointed Grant Thornton to take control of the Ta Xbiex-based online trading platform Trive Financial Services, whose clients have been left unable to access their money. The Turkish-owned firm was left without a board after a spate of top-level resignations left it unable to operate; if the business cannot be salvaged, Grant Thornton will wind it up on the MFSAs instructions. The move follows a 10-year ban on shareholder Kasim Garipoglu from operating in Maltas regulated financial services sector.

item.title: Femicide observatory: partners linked to 24 of 55 women killed since 1970
item.description: The Malta Observatory on Femicide says a current partner killed 24 of the 55 women it has identified as femicide victims in Malta between January 1970 and September 2026, with an ex-partner responsible for 13 more. Twenty-seven of the victims were killed in their own home, and 93% of the perpetrators were male. The figures are not official statistics, as Malta has no national femicide dataset, and the observatory compiles its count from public sources.
